AI News Daily — 15 Nov 2026

TOP STORY: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on one underlying model, cutting Fable's API price to $8 / $40 per million tokens and limiting Mythos to vetted cyber-defence users. Google answered with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast daily driver at $1.50 / $7.50 per million tokens with a 1M context and an Orchestrator that swaps it for the larger Carbon mid-session.

5 KEY UPDATES
1. Open weights surge: Moonshot Kimi K3.1 Pro (1M context, 3T scale), Meituan LongCat-2.5 (1.6T MoE, 48B active), Tencent Hunyuan Hy4 (770B, can operate a computer), Alibaba Qwen3.5, and Edge0-145B running on a laptop with no licence named.
2. Agentic commerce arrives: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay with network tokens after a Face ID or fingerprint check, starting with US Pro subscribers.
3. Anthropic's IPO roadshow is winding up with compute commitments at the centre; AirTrunk signed an MoU for 1.8GW of data centre capacity in Andhra Pradesh, India.
4. Nvidia is run by an interim CEO after Jensen Huang's resignation, with tech executives petitioning for his reinstatement and chip export scrutiny heading to Congress in December.
5. Safety: Cursor's post-mortem shows a leaked vendor key put a poisoned Claude Code extension in front of ~5,000 developers, and four nonprofits sued OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and SpaceX to freeze frontier development.

CONCEPT OF THE DAY: The cheap layer is where the stack is being decided. Fast models, routers and stopping rules now matter more than another benchmark point — research this week found a median 35-60% of a successful coding agent's steps happen after the correct patch is already in place.

Full briefing: https://dilip457.github.io/ai-news-daily/
